stem: Emma needs to choose one person at random from three people, $P$, $Q$ and $R$. She plans to throw two fair coins and note the number, $n$, of heads. If $n$ is 0, she will choose $P$. If $n$ is 1, she will choose $Q$. If $n$ is 2, she will choose $R$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: By considering probabilities, show that the choice made by this method is not random.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Later, Emma has to choose two people at random from three people.
parts.text: Describe how Emma could use a single throw of a fair six-sided dice to make this random choice.
